runs.name: EVI Industries, Inc.
runs.entry: Price **$19.20** (2026-10-12, live quote from `tools/run.py`, aggregator, flagged) x **12,878,532 shares** (one class; 10-K cover as of 2026-09-03, 0001437749-26-029759; checked against 13,151,783 issued less 276,087 treasury at 2026-06-30, the 2,836 difference employee plan issuance; the Sudsies transactions amended 2026-08-31 to all cash, no shares issued, 8-Ks 0001437749-26-024286 and 0001437749-26-029515) = cap **$247.3M**; sovereign **5.60%** (UST 30Y, 2026-10-09). Primary document the FY2026 10-K (0001437749-26-029759), with the FY2019 to FY2025 10-Ks, the DEF 14A of 2025-11-20 (0002077096-25-000183) and the 8-Ks of 2026-07-23, 2026-09-02 and 2026-09-08; FY2026 operating cash $20,606 thousand cross-checked to the filed cash-flow statement and revenue $446,570 thousand to the press release. A value-added distributor of commercial laundry equipment made by others, with installation, maintenance and repair, grown by a buy-and-build programme; formerly EnviroStar and DRYCLEAN USA. Lines of evidence derived by the analyst from the 10-K's Items 1, 1A and 7, as the overnight brief directs (supplier dependence, the basis of competition, growth by acquisition, and more listed in the run). `tools/run.py` skipped FY2024 in its three-year owner-cash table because the capital-spending tag changed; the series was rebuilt from the filed statements. **Q1 IN** (the economics of a distributor of slowly changing equipment understood). **Q2 OUT**: the castle is shown open: the money test answered yes by the company's own record (one Miami distributor with 31 employees in 2015 made "North America's leading" distributor by about $117M of cash acquisitions and $76.4M of stock to sellers, in a field of more than 500 distributors where no competitor has a major share) and by Alliance Laundry, the largest North American maker, buying four distributors in 2024 to 2025, one in New York the month EVI bought one there; the local exclusivity is the suppliers' to grant (four manufacturers 71% of purchases, contracts terminable on short notice, supplier relationships that "ceased" on certain acquisitions in every 10-K from FY2019, Alliance listed as a major supplier in FY2020 and gone from FY2021); "competitive pricing" a stated basis of competition; operating margin 5.7% in FY2017 and 3.5% in FY2026, not widened with scale. Q3 to Q12 not reached. Integrity facts recorded, not judged: headline Adjusted EBITDA excludes stock pay; the July 2026 release overstated Sudsies' EBITDA growth as 62%, corrected to 31% in the covering 8-K; a controlled company, management and board directing 52.3% of the vote; CEO pay $5.35M against net income $7.5M (FY2025) and $5.91M against $5.6M (FY2024); a $10M buyback authorization with no price. Evidence against the box set down by the analyst: pretax return on tangible capital about 11% to 27% (2.7% to 10.7% on total capital including purchased goodwill), gross margin up from 23.1% to 31.5%, long-term distribution agreements credited in the proxy, 55,000 customers and a service network. Beneath the stop, COMPUTATION, NOT A CLEARANCE: owner cash FY2022 to FY2026 averages $5.70M a year before acquisitions and -$8.36M after cash acquisitions; net debt $81.6M ($44.2M at 2026-06-30 plus the $37.4M cash paid for Sudsies on 2026-09-01, credited at nothing for want of filed earnings; at its press-release operating income after a 25% tax labelled a CONVENTION of the run it would add $4.89 a share); a sign-changing series, so one no-growth case: value **-$4.35** a share all-equity (-$2.12 equity-only; ten-year base -$4.49), fair **-$7.35** all-equity (-$3.31 equity-only); organic pair beside $3.83 value, -$0.64 fair all-equity ($6.07 and $3.40 equity-only); no positive all-equity fair price, not armed. Balance sheets FY2016 to FY2026: assets $10M to $304M; of the $145M rise in equity $37M retained earnings, the rest mostly stock to sellers; goodwill and intangibles $122.8M, 82% of equity, tangible equity about $27M; inventory 18% of sales in 2022, released in FY2024; debt $8.8M to $53M with the acquisitions. Competitors: the 10-K names none; the analyst used Alliance Laundry (operating margin 17.3% to 18.8%, 2023 to 2025, a maker that owns distribution, not like for like) and Alta Equipment as a stand-in dealer roll-up in another field (-0.9% to 2.9%, 2019 to 2025) against EVI's 1.2% to 5.7% (FY2017 to FY2026). Contamination declared by the analyst: a listing of `Test Runs/` filtered by the date (nine other runs of the day seen by name, none opened), commit subjects in the session context, and the inference from the project map that a v4.1 run may exist; nothing used. Commits 2a41bc4c to 357b64c1. Citations: the analyst's check 36 ids, 16 fragments, 0 problems; the dispatcher's adjacency script (`dispatcher_check2.py`) 36 ids present, 14 adjacent fragments, 0 slips. Position note filled at the fold. check_framework PASS. Analyst's gaps for the operator: (1) specific (c)'s default pair with zero growth credited from year one: the text does not say whether acquisitions are still deducted for ten years (the analyst did, showing the organic pair beside) or stop at once; a run near the price would turn on it; (2) the framework does not say what substitute competitor to use when the 10-K names none; (3) Q2's ordinary-returns convention does not say whether a roll-up's return is read on tangible capital or on total capital including purchased goodwill, which give opposite readings here; (4) a deal closed after the window has only press-release figures, not a filed record, and was credited at nothing; (5) `tools/run.py`'s three-year owner-cash mean silently skips a year when the capital-spending tag changes. Not obtained: audited Sudsies financials, organic growth (not reported), a maintenance and growth split of capital spending, more than three years of Alliance figures.
runs.narr: Q2 OUT: the castle is shown open; a single Miami distributor of 2015 bought its way to North America's leading laundry distributor in a field of more than 500, the largest maker is buying distributors too, the local exclusivity is the suppliers' to grant on short notice, price is a stated basis of competition, and operating margin fell from 5.7% to 3.5% as it grew. Integrity facts recorded: adjusted EBITDA excluding stock pay, a corrected overstatement of Sudsies' growth, a controlled company, CEO pay near net income. COMPUTATION beneath the stop: fair -$7.35 all-equity (-$3.31 equity-only) against $19.20 (not armed). The analyst asks whether acquisitions are still deducted when no growth is credited, and on which capital a roll-up's ordinary return is read.
